summary: Three of the four pinned packages have published advisories: lodash 4.17.15, requests 2.19.0 and Flask 3.0.3. dayjs 1.11.13 has none. I re-queried requests: OSV returned 10 advisories, not 11, so the earlier count of 11 was wrong and all 10 IDs are now listed.

findings.title: lodash 4.17.15 has 6 known advisories
findings.evidence: "lodash": "4.17.15". OSV returned 6 advisories. The worst is GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, code injection via _.template imports key names (CVSS v3 AV:N/AC:H/PR:N, C/I/A High, base 8.1). GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm, command injection, scores 7.2. Also returned: prototype pollution (GHSA-p6mc-m468-83gw, GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg) and ReDoS (GHSA-29mw-wpgm-hmr9).
findings.recommendation: The lowest fixed version above 4.17.15 is 4.17.19, which fixes only GHSA-p6mc-m468-83gw. 4.17.21 also fixes the ReDoS and command injection advisories. 4.18.0 is the lowest version that fixes all six, including the two 2026 advisories. Upgrade to 4.18.0 or later.

findings.title: requests 2.19.0 has 10 known advisories
findings.evidence: requests==2.19.0. OSV returned 10 advisories: 5 GHSA entries and 5 PYSEC duplicates of them, covering 5 distinct issues. The worst is GHSA-x84v-xcm2-53pg / PYSEC-2018-28 (CVE-2018-18074), credentials sent in the Authorization header on an https-to-http redirect (CVSS v3 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/C:H, base 7.5). Others: .netrc credential leak, verify=False session bypass, Proxy-Authorization leak, and insecure temp file reuse in extract_zipped_paths.
findings.recommendation: The lowest fixed version above 2.19.0 is 2.20.0, which fixes only the CVE-2018-18074 pair. The highest fixed version is 2.33.0, which fixes all 10 advisories. Upgrade to 2.33.0 or later.

findings.title: Flask 3.0.3 missing Vary: Cookie header advisory
findings.evidence: Flask==3.0.3. GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726 / PYSEC-2026-2151: the session does not add a Vary: Cookie header when accessed in some ways. The CVSS v3 score for PYSEC-2026-2151 is 4.3 (medium). The v4 vector on GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726 has VC:L only, so its rating is estimated as medium.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Flask 3.1.3 or later, the lowest fixed version above 3.0.3.

limitations: express ("*", package.json line 7) and gunicorn (no version, requirements.txt line 3) have no exact version, so I could not query them. The dependency_hygiene step covers them.
No lockfile exists, so versions come from the manifests only.

challenge_responses.rationale: I re-queried requests 2.19.0. OSV returned 10 advisories, not 11. The earlier count was wrong, and advisory_ids now lists all 10 returned IDs.
The recommendations now name the lowest fixed version above the pinned one: 4.17.19 for lodash and 2.20.0 for requests. Each also names the version that fixes every advisory: 4.18.0 and 2.33.0.
